topology_reasoning: The target is not a single connected splitter tree; it is three separate black waveguide bodies arranged vertically.
The middle body is a long left-anchored taper/arm that stays centered vertically and terminates before the right edge.

The upper and lower bodies are mirror-symmetric S-bent tapers: they begin as narrow straight stubs near x≈124 px, widen gradually, then bend away from the center near the right side while keeping roughly constant final width.
The function-defining knobs are the waveguide width, taper length, the location where the outer S-bends begin, the bend span/radius, and the gap/vertical offsets between the three arms.
The geometry should be modeled from primitives only: straight segments, tapers, and smooth bends assembled parametrically.

iterations.change_made: Initial primitive draft placed all three arms too early and used a single blunt taper model.
Moved the upper/lower arms to start at x≈3.07 um, fixed taper placement, and aligned the main layout bbox.
Tested a more aggressive outer-arm bend profile and an alternate center-arm construction; this over-shot the shape and reduced overlap.
Reverted the center arm to a single taper and kept the more accurate outer-arm profile.
Shifted the middle arm upward by 0.016 um, changed delta_length so only the upper arm responds, and flattened the export so verify_knob_response sees layer-(1,0) area.
